4546	\subsection{Precision and exact recovery}
4547	
4548	Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} uses
4549	$C_1=20$, so $\epsilon C_1<1$ makes its coefficient width $O(p)$.
4550	Lemma~\ref{lem:synthetic-transform-cost} therefore applies to every
4551	synthetic transform here, with error less than
4552	$\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}<L2^{-p}$, where $L=\log_2T$, for all
4553	sufficiently large $n$.
4554	
4555	\subsubsection{Scales and disk margins}
4556	
4557	Put $h_p=2^{-p}$, and use the coefficient sup norm throughout this
4558	subsection.  An error of $a$ will mean absolute error less than $ah_p$.
4559	A linear contraction propagates an input error without increasing it.
4560	For a bilinear contraction $\mathcal M$, replacing its operands gives
4561	\[
4562	 \|\mathcal M(f',g')-\mathcal M(f,g)\|
4563	 \le \|f'-f\|\,\|g'\|+\|f\|\,\|g'-g\|.
4564	\]
4565	When all four operands are in the disk, their two errors therefore add.
4566	
4567	We also need the norm as well as the error of a computed phase product.
4568	Let $e$ be a unit phase, let $\widetilde e$ be a disk-grid approximation
4569	with $|\widetilde e-e|<2h_p$, and let $x$ be a disk operand.  The
4570	truncation bound in \eqref{eq:transform-truncate} gives
4571	\[
4572	 \|Q_p(\widetilde e x)-ex\|
4573	   <(2\|x\|+\sqrt2)h_p<4h_p,
4574	 \qquad
4575	 \|Q_p(\widetilde e x)\|\le\|x\|.
4576	\]
4577	The second inequality follows from $|\widetilde e|\le1$ and the fact
4578	that $Q_p$ does not increase the norm.  It preserves every smaller
4579	operand norm through a twist or an endpoint phase multiplication.
4580	The same bounds hold coordinatewise for arrays of phases.
4581	
4582	For disk-grid ring arrays $f,g$, put $M=T/r$.  Two normalized synthetic
4583	forwards, pointwise polynomial multiplication divided by $r$, and the
4584	normalized opposite transform give $(f*g)/(rM^2)$.  The exact
4585	multiplication by $M$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:synthetic-convolution}
4586	then gives $\mathcal M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T$.  Before that multiplication,
4587	the three transform errors and the polynomial-product truncation total
4588	less than $3L+2$.  Thus the error of the returned normalized
4589	convolution is bounded by
4590	\[
4591	 E_{\rm ring}:=M(3L+2)<5TL.
4592	\]
4593	If one operand has norm at most $.7$, bilinear contraction gives
4594	$\|\mathcal M_r(f,g)\|\le.7$.  Its computed grid output consequently
4595	has norm less than $.7+5TLh_p<.701$ for large $n$.  This proves the
4596	disk margin after the scale $M$, without clipping the output.
4597	
4598	Consider now $\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(f,g)$ for disk grid
4599	operands, one of norm at most $.7$.  Its two computed input twists
4600	$f',g'$ are disk grid arrays, and the smaller one still has norm at
4601	most $.7$ by the phase inequality.  The identification $\iota$
4602	preserves these bounds.  The preceding ring margin therefore gives
4603	$\|h'\|<.701$.  Neither $\iota^{-1}$ nor the computed output untwist
4604	increases this norm.  In particular,
4605	$\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(f,g)$ is a disk grid array.
4606	
4607	To compare it with $\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)$, insert the exact
4608	normalized $\mathcal M_r$ at $\iota f'$ and $\iota g'$.
4609	Its bilinear contraction bound propagates the two input twist errors,
4610	each less than $4$.  Its approximation contributes $E_{\rm ring}$,
4611	and the output untwist contributes less than $4$.  All these

4613	factor $M$.  They give
4614	\[
4615	 \|\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathbb C}(f,g)
4616	            -\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g)\|
4617	 <(E_{\rm ring}+4+4+4)h_p<6TLh_p.
4618	\]

4621	defined data operand $x_0=Q_p(\overline{\widetilde a}\cdot x)$ has
4622	norm at most $.6$.  The kernel $\widetilde a$ is a disk grid array.
4623	Thus this pair satisfies the smaller-operand condition just proved:
4624	$\|y_0\|<.701$, and the last endpoint multiplication gives
4625	$\|\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)\|<.701$.  In particular, the chirp output
4626	is a legal disk-grid input to the compression maps.

4628	For its error, the exact operands $a$ and $\overline a\cdot x$ are in
4629	the disk because every entry of $a$ has modulus one.  The kernel
4630	approximation contributes less than $2$ and
4631	the first endpoint multiplication contributes less than $4$ when
4632	inserted into the exact bilinear contraction
4633	$\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}$.  The computed convolution contributes less
4634	than $6TL$, and the last endpoint multiplication less than $4$.

4636	\[
4637	 \|\widetilde{\mathscr C}(x)-QF_{\boldsymbol t}x\|
4638	 <(6TL+2+4+4)h_p<8TLh_p.
4639	\]
4640	
4641	Finally let the input to a source transform have norm at most $.5$.
4642	The computed expansion has error less than $dp^2$ and norm less than
4643	$.5+dp^2h_p<.51$.  It is therefore a permitted chirp input.  The
4644	chirp output is in the disk by the preceding argument, so each
4645	compression call is defined and returns another disk-grid array.
4646	Insert the exact contractions $\mathcal A$, $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$,
4647	and $\mathcal B_0$ at the computed inputs.  The error before the
4648	source scale is less than $2dp^2+8TL$.  Multiplication by
4649	$2^\gamma$ therefore gives error less than
4650	$2^\gamma(2dp^2+8TL)h_p$, which is bounded by $E_sh_p$ with
4651	\begin{equation}\label{eq:source-error}
4652	 E_s=9\,2^\gamma TL,
4653	\end{equation}
4654	because $2dp^2<TL$ eventually.  The exact source transform
4655	$RF_{\boldsymbol s}$ is a contraction, so the scaled approximation
4656	has norm at most $.5+E_sh_p<.501$.  Its exact numerator scaling
4657	therefore also leaves a disk-grid output without clipping.
4658	Conjugation preserves the grid and norm, so the opposite procedure
4659	has the same error and disk guarantee.
4660	All these margins may be enforced by one fixed cutoff.  For example,
4661	$b\ge2^{24}$, together with the other eventual construction conditions,
4662	makes $dp^2h_p$, $8TLh_p$, $E_sh_p$ and
4663	$28\,2^\gamma T^2Lh_p$ smaller than $10^{-3}$.
4664	
4665	\subsubsection{The final integer coefficients}
4666	
4667	The scaled radix digits in $u,v$ are exact $p$-bit grid values of norm
4668	strictly less than $1/4$.  Put
4669	\[
4670	 \begin{aligned}
4671	 U&=RF_{\boldsymbol s}u,&\qquad V_1&=RF_{\boldsymbol s}v,\\
4672	 \widetilde U&=\widetilde{\mathscr F}(u),&
4673	 \widetilde V_1&=\widetilde{\mathscr F}(v).
4674	 \end{aligned}
4675	\]
4676	The exact arrays have norm less than $1/4$, and the computed arrays
4677	have norm less than $1/4+E_sh_p<.26$.  Hence
4678	$z=Q_p(\widetilde U\cdot\widetilde V_1)$ has norm at most
4679	$.26^2<.5$.  To estimate its error, write
4680	\[
4681	 \widetilde U\cdot\widetilde V_1-U\cdot V_1
4682	 =(\widetilde U-U)\cdot\widetilde V_1
4683	       +U\cdot(\widetilde V_1-V_1).
4684	\]
4685	The factors $\widetilde V_1$ and $U$ are in the disk.  The two terms
4686	have total norm less than $2E_sh_p$, and truncation adds less than $2h_p$.
4687	Thus $\|z-U\cdot V_1\|<(2E_s+2)h_p$.
4688	
4689	Let $G:=RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ be the exact opposite contraction.
4690	Lemma~\ref{lem:chirp-permutation}, applied to
4691	$U=RF_{\boldsymbol s}u$ and $V_1=RF_{\boldsymbol s}v$, gives
4692	\[
4693	 G(U\cdot V_1)=(u*v)/S^2.
4694	\]
4695	The computed opposite transform may be applied to $z$ because
4696	$\|z\|<.5$. Insert $G$ at that computed input:
4697	\[
4698	 \begin{aligned}
4699	 \|\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)-G(U\cdot V_1)\|
4700	 &\le \|\widetilde{\mathscr F}^{+}(z)-Gz\|\\
4701	 &\qquad+\|G(z-U\cdot V_1)\|\\
4702	 &<(3E_s+2)h_p.
4703	 \end{aligned}
4704	\]
4705	The first exact numerator multiplication by $S$ gives
4706	$\widetilde w$, approximating $w=(u*v)/S$ with error less than
4707	$E_wh_p$, where
4708	\[
4709	 E_w:=S(3E_s+2)<28\,2^\gamma T^2L.
4710	\]
4711	Each coefficient of $w$ is an average of $S$ products of coefficients
4712	of $u$ and $v$, so $\|w\|<1/16$.  The earlier cutoff therefore gives
4713	\[
4714	 \|\widetilde w\|<1/16+E_wh_p<1/16+10^{-3}<1.
4715	\]
4716	This proves the disk bound for the computed first scaled result.
4717	
4718	In tensor order, the unscaled integer coefficient array is
4719	$2^{2b+4}S w$.  This second occurrence of $S$ reverses the
4720	normalization still present in $w$, and $2^{2b+4}$ reverses the two
4721	input scales.  Both multiplications act exactly on grid numerators.
4722	Since $S\le T<2^b$ and $L<b$ eventually, the final absolute error is less than
4723	\begin{equation}\label{eq:final-error}
4724	 2^{2b+4}S\cdot28\,2^\gamma T^2L\cdot2^{-6b}
4725	 <448b\,2^{-b+\gamma}
4726	 \le448b\,2^{-3b/4}<\frac12.
4727	\end{equation}
4728	The true coefficients are real integers.  If $H_j$ is the real
4729	numerator after the second scaling, its represented value is
4730	$H_j/2^p$.  The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to
4731	that value the unique correct coefficient.
4732	
4733	These exact operations use known fixed record widths. If $N$ is a
4734	signed $w_0$-bit integer, then $-2^{w_0-1}\leq N<2^{w_0-1}$. Since
4735	$0<S<2^b$, its product satisfies
4736	$-2^{w_0+b-1}<SN<2^{w_0+b-1}$ and therefore fits in signed width $w_0+b$.
4737	The first product by $S$ starts at width $w_{\rm c}$ and is written in
4738	width $w_{\rm c}+b$. The next product by $S$ is written in width
4739	$w_{\rm c}+2b$; appending $2b+4$ least significant zero bits then gives
4740	the exact second scale in width $w_{\rm c}+4b+4$. Each complex record
4741	still places its most-significant-bit-first real word before its imaginary
4742	word. The known widths determine every boundary in the next scan and are
4743	$O(p)$ because $p=6b$.
4744	
4745	The established integer multiplier performs the two products by $S$ in
4746	$O(p\log p)$ time per entry. To serialize each exact signed product at
4747	its stated width, zero-pad its magnitude and complement and increment
4748	for a negative sign. The proved bounds ensure that no significant bit is
4749	discarded. These conversions and the power-of-two shift use linear scans.
4750	To round $H_j/2^p$, recover the real magnitude, inspect its low $p$ bits,
4751	and apply the rounding carry with the sign restored. The strict error
4752	bound makes the result the correct nonnegative coefficient, and
4753	\eqref{eq:capacity} puts it in $[0,2^{3b})$. It therefore fits in one
4754	signed $(3b+1)$-bit two's-complement word, written most significant bit
4755	first. Scan the padded box in the
4756	physical axis order recorded by its shape descriptor, using the same
4757	$O(p)$-bit nested counters and validity tests as above. Consume the
4758	imaginary word and write this real coefficient word at each valid address,
4759	with an all-zero
4760	word at each padded address. This serialization costs $O(Tp)$ in total.
4761	It keeps the tensor address order and supplies payload width $3b+1$ to
4762	the local descriptors for $\Phi^{-1}$, so the address routine receives a
4763	stream of known fixed-length records.
4764	
4765	Lemma~\ref{lem:signed-ring-product} proves exact signed packing,
4766	centered extraction and negacyclic reduction. Its only numerical error
4767	is the stated truncation after division by $r$, already included above.
4768	Undo the coefficient-address isomorphism $\Phi$ before propagating
4769	radix carries.
4770	
4771	To propagate carries, let $Q_0=2^b$.  The recovered ordinary
4772	coefficients are the $c_j$ in \eqref{eq:capacity}; they are zero for
4773	$2q-2<j<S$.  With $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ as
4774	above, use the recurrence for $0\le j<S$:
4775	\[
4776	 k_0=0,\qquad d_j=(c_j+k_j)\bmod Q_0,\qquad
4777	 k_{j+1}=\left\lfloor\frac{c_j+k_j}{Q_0}\right\rfloor.
4778	\]
4779	The carries satisfy $0\le k_j\le q(Q_0-1)<Q_0^2$.  If this holds at
4780	$j$, then
4781	\[
4782	 c_j+k_j\le q(Q_0-1)^2+q(Q_0-1)=qQ_0(Q_0-1),
4783	\]
4784	which proves the next carry bound.  The defining relation
4785	$c_j+k_j=d_j+Q_0k_{j+1}$ also gives the exact invariant
4786	\[
4787	 \sum_{h<j}c_hQ_0^h
4788	   =\sum_{h<j}d_hQ_0^h+k_jQ_0^j.
4789	\]
4790	It holds for $j=0$, and the defining relation proves its next instance.
4791	The unprocessed terms are multiples of $Q_0^j$, so the identity fixes
4792	the first $j$ radix digits of the full product.  The value $k_j$ is
4793	the carry from the processed coefficients into the remaining positions.
4794	
4795	After $\Phi^{-1}$ the coefficients occur in increasing ordinary index,
4796	so this carry scan proceeds from least to most significant.  Carry
4797	storage and work per coefficient are $O(b)$ bits and steps.  Write
4798	each digit's bits from low to high on a work tape, and drain the final
4799	$O(b)$-bit carry in the same order.  Copy the completed stream backward
4800	once to obtain most-significant-first order.  The stream has length
4801	$O(Sb)=O(Tp)$, including chunk padding and the final carry, so this
4802	reversal is a charged linear tape pass.  The exact product is less
4803	than $2^{2n}$; all bits above position $2n-1$ are therefore zero.
4804	Remove only those zero padding bits and retain leading zeros as needed
4805	to produce exactly $2n$ bits.  Zero inputs obey the same invariant and
4806	output rule.
4807	
4808	\subsection{The complete time bound}
4809	
4810	For the cost calculation put $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$. The fixed-width coefficient
4811	formats use $\Theta(p)$ bits per coefficient, so a full padded array has
4812	$\Theta(V)$ stored bits. Table~\ref{tab:costs} lists costs after division
4813	by $V$; a fixed number of repeated transforms and convolutions is
4814	included in its constants.
4815	\begin{table}[ht]
4816	\centering
4817	\small
4818	\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.40\linewidth}ll@{}}
4819	\toprule
4820	Operation & Normalized cost & Power of $p$\\
4821	\midrule
4822	Prefix-slot moves and individual butterfly rounds & $dK$ & $\epsilon(1+c)$\\
4823	Chunk exchanges for transform layout & $pK^{\tau-1}$ & $1-\epsilon c(1-\tau)$\\
4824	Simultaneous butterfly rounds & $\ell d^{\lambda'}$ & $1-\epsilon(1-\lambda')$\\
4825	CRT and axis layouts & $d^2(1+\ell^\tau)$ & $\tau+\epsilon(2-\tau)$\\
4826	Gaussian line maps & $dp^{1/2+\delta}\alpha$ & $3/4+\delta+3\epsilon/2$\\
4827	Chirps, twists and scalar products & $dp^\delta$ & $\epsilon+\delta$\\
4828	Packed polynomial products & $\log(rp)$ & $1-\epsilon$\\
4829	Final scaling and rounding & $p^\delta$ & absorbed above\\
4830	Input, padding, carries and output & $1$ & absorbed above\\
4831	\bottomrule
4832	\end{tabular}
4833	\caption{Costs divided by $Tp$; each coefficient
4834	representation has $O(p)$ bits.}\label{tab:costs}
4835	\end{table}
4836	
4837	The seven dominant powers in Table~\ref{tab:costs} have the following
4838	margins below one:
4839	\begin{equation}\label{eq:margin-list}
4840	\begin{split}
4841	 g_1&=1-\epsilon(1+c),\qquad
4842	 g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau),\qquad
4843	 g_3=\epsilon(1-\lambda'),\\
4844	 g_4&=1-\tau-\epsilon(2-\tau),\qquad
4845	 g_5=1/4-\delta-3\epsilon/2,\\
4846	 g_6&=1-\delta-\epsilon,\qquad g_7=\epsilon.
4847	\end{split}
4848	\end{equation}
4849	Direct substitution gives
4850	\[
4851	 g_1>\frac12,\quad g_2=2^{-181},\quad g_3=2^{-129},\quad
4852	 g_4>2^{-51},\quad g_5>\frac18,\quad g_6>\frac12,\quad g_7=2^{-75}.
4853	\]
4854	Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.  This explicit slack will cover
4855	any remaining fixed power of $\log p$.
4856	
4857	Here $d^2$ is absorbed by $d^2\ell^\tau$, and
4858	$\log(rp)=O(p^{1-\epsilon}+\log p)=O(p^{1-\epsilon})$.
4859	The first three rows are the terms in
4860	\eqref{eq:synthetic-transform-cost}. The prefix-slot moves and
4861	individual butterfly rounds in Lemma~\ref{lem:synthetic-transform-cost}
4862	use $O(dK)$ linear scans. Its positional layout uses $O(p/K)$ exchanges
4863	of width-$K$ chunks, because $d\ell=O(p)$. Each exchange costs
4864	$O(VK^\tau)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:chunk-swap}, so the normalized total is
4865	\[
4866	 O(p/K)\,K^\tau=O(pK^{\tau-1}).
4867	\]
4868	For the at most $\ell$ simultaneous rounds,
4869	Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} supplies $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$
4870	per round. Its bound already includes the binary basis changes,
4871	deterministic repair, row padding and removal, all base-$m$ groups,
4872	and fixed-tape cleanup.
4873	
4874	Axis exposure and restoration require $O(d^2)$ adjacent axis moves.
4875	Each costs $O(V(1+\ell^\tau))$: peel a single excess bit when widths
4876	differ by one, exchange their equal-width parts, and restore the bit.
4877	The $d$ CRT rotations copy valid and invalid intervals in $O(dV)$ time.
4878	Their offset setup was bounded above by $O(dTp^C/r)=o(Tp)$,
4879	using at most $T/t_i$ control prefixes for target $i$.
4880	
4881	For Gaussian resampling, axis $i$ has at most $T/t_i$ processed lines.
4882	The line-machine costs therefore sum to
4883	\[
4884	 \sum_{i=1}^d\frac{T}{t_i}
4885	       O(t_i p^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)
4886	 =O(dTp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha).
4887	\]
4888	Dividing by $V=Tp$ gives the fifth row.  The factor
4889	$\alpha=\Theta(p^{1/4+\epsilon/2})$ explains its displayed power of $p$.
4890	
4891	Chirp numerators have $O(p)$ bits and can be computed modulo $2r$ as
4892	sums of $d$ terms $s_i j_i^2(r/t_i)$.  Computing their squares and
4893	products with the previously established $O(N\log(2N))$ multiplier
4894	on $N$-bit inputs,
4895	then generating the exponentials, costs $O(dp^{1+\delta})$ per entry.
4896	The smaller twist and scalar pointwise-product costs fit the same row:
4897	they use a fixed number of exact products on $O(p)$-bit component
4898	numerators, followed by linear truncation scans.  The two final products
4899	by $S$ also cost $O(p\log p)$ per entry, so their normalized cost is
4900	$O(\log p)=O(p^\delta)$ as listed separately.  There are $T/r$
4901	polynomial records in each pointwise ring product.  Four integer
4902	products on $O(rp)$ bits per record therefore cost
4903	$O(Tp\log(rp))$ in total.  Signed packing, centered extraction,
4904	negacyclic wrapping, and copying are linear stream passes.  These calls
4905	use the previously established multiplier on records of length
4906	$O(rp)=o(n)$; they do not call the improved algorithm being constructed.
4907	The exact source scaling by $2^\gamma$ is a shift of $O(p)$-bit
4908	numerators by $\gamma=O(p)$ places, so it is a linear scan per entry
4909	and fits the final-scaling row. The scalar-format adapters and the exact
4910	removal of sign-extension bits after the ring and source scales also use
4911	linear scans of their $O(p)$-bit components, within the listed scan costs.
4912	
4913	\paragraph{Setup and exceptional streams across all calls.}
4914	We next separate setup at recursion nodes from work repeated for every
4915	polynomial record or every Gaussian line.  Here a visit means a node
4916	of the layer or address-layout recursions, or one of their round and
4917	group invocations.  The internal recursion of the established integer
4918	multiplier and the iterations of the quoted Gaussian algorithms are
4919	already included in their separately charged running times.
4920	The layer and address-layout recursions have constant branching and
4921	depth $O(\log p)$, and the number of their rounds and base-$m$ groups
4922	is polynomial in $p$.  Choose a fixed exponent $A$ so that their
4923	total number of visits is at most $p^A$, and a fixed $C$ bounding
4924	descriptor setup performed once per visit by $p^C$ steps.  This setup then
4925	costs at most $p^{A+C}=o(Tp)$.
4926	
4927	At a layer or synthetic-transform visit that processes polynomial
4928	records, there are at most $O(T/r)$ such records, including the
4929	bounded row padding.  Every relevant child keeps the whole
4930	length-$r$ polynomial suffix.  Consequently $O(p^C)$ descriptor or
4931	address work per record, over these visits, costs at most
4932	$O(Tp^{A+C}/r)=o(Tp)$.  Setup before each Gaussian line call has a
4933	different count:
4934	there are at most $2dT/r$ lines per tensor map and only a fixed number
4935	of such maps, so $O(p^C)$ setup per line costs
4936	$O(dTp^C/r)=o(Tp)$.  These estimates all use that $r$ exceeds every
4937	fixed power of $p$.
4938	
4939	The general address-swap subroutine also covers one-bit payloads,
4940	where no polynomial suffix is available. For root volume $V_0$ and
4941	current child volume $V_j$, the descriptor estimate in the proof of
4942	Proposition~\ref{prop:power-interchange} gives
4943	$(\log(2V_0))^{O(1)}=O(V_j)$. It uses the invariant that both original
4944	chunk ranges remain present in every child, and therefore includes
4945	polynomial descriptor work even for a one-bit payload.
4946	Elementary counter updates use local length copies, so they do not
4947	rescan a growing descriptor for each data bit.  The chirp computation
4948	does scan the axis descriptors at every coefficient; its
4949	$O(Tdp^{1+\delta})$ cost was included in the chirp row.
4950	
4951	For one packed change of basis, let $V_{\rm call}$ be its current
4952	logical volume.  The bad-address fraction is
4953	$O(d2^{-K})$, independently of the payload.  Each polynomial record
4954	has $\Theta(rp)$ payload bits, and an exceptional record adds an
4955	$O(p)$-bit destination key.  Thus the compact exceptional stream has
4956	length
4957	\[
4958	 O\!\left(\frac{V_{\rm call}}{rp}\,d2^{-K}(rp+p)\right)
4959	   =O(V_{\rm call}d2^{-K}).
4960	\]
4961	Stable bit sorting makes $O(p)$ scans of this stream, for one-call
4962	cost $O(V_{\rm call}dp2^{-K})$.  Extraction and reinsertion use a
4963	constant number of scans of the full current volume; those scans are
4964	already in the node overhead.  Since there are at most $p^A$ visits,
4965	each of volume $O(V)$, the compact sorting costs sum to at most
4966	\[
4967	 O\!\left(dp2^{-K}\sum_{\rm calls}V_{\rm call}\right)
4968	   =O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V)
4969	\]
4970	for another fixed exponent $A'$.  Here $d=O(p^\epsilon)$ and
4971	$K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ with $\epsilon c>0$.  Predicate and key
4972	arithmetic is the polynomial work per record counted above.  This is
4973	a deterministic worst-case bound.
4974	
4975	Finally, all role, arithmetic, and stack tapes form fixed finite
4976	families.  A child parks and restores only its parent's streams, with
4977	the stack head at the active top; copying and cleanup are charged to
4978	that logical volume.  No operation repeatedly scans parked ancestors.
4979	Growing axis lists and call states are stored data, not extra tapes or
4980	alphabet symbols.  Global setup and prime search cost $o(V)$, as
4981	proved earlier.
4982	
4983	Each of the seven displayed powers is at most $1-2\kappa$ by
4984	\eqref{eq:margin-list}.  Any fixed power of $\log p$ is at most $p^\kappa$
4985	eventually.  The complete large-input bound is consequently
4986	\[
4987	 O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}).
4988	\]
4989	Fix one cutoff beyond all the size, precision, margin and layout
4990	conditions, and use schoolbook multiplication below it.  The finitely
4991	many smaller lengths are included by enlarging the implicit constant.
4992	With $\lg n=\max\{\lceil\log_2n\rceil,1\}$, the resulting single
4993	fixed-alphabet, fixed-tape deterministic machine has worst-case time
4994	$O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ for every input length and produces precisely
4995	the required $2n$-bit product.
4996	 \section{Exact division and integer square root}
4997	\label{sec:exact-arithmetic-proof}
4998	
4999	Let $n$ be the supplied input width, let $a$ be the nonnegative dividend
5000	or radicand, and let $b>0$ be the divisor for the division task, with
5001	the values and output conventions of Corollary~\ref{cor:exact-arithmetic}.
5002	Here $p\ge1$ denotes an integer target precision for a Newton routine.
